# <span id="aanchor347"></span> Tank Editor - Flow Data

[&lt;&lt; Back](../Tank%20Editor.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Gauging</a> \| [Tickets](Tank%20Editor_Flow%20-%20Tickets.md) \| [Daily](Tank%20Editor_Flow%20-%20Daily.md) \| [Monthly](Tank%20Editor_Flow%20-%20Monthly.md)

#### Gauging Tab

The Gauging tab displays the gauge levels associated with gauge tickets or run tickets currently attached to the tank for the specified time period. Double-click record to open the associated ticket for viewing or editing.

Gauge tickets can be created and deleted from the Gauging tab.

<div class="procedure">

To enter a gauge ticket:

1.  Navigate to the Tank Editor and select a tank.

2.  Click the **Gauging** tab

3.  Right-click the grid and select **New Tank Level**.

4.  Navigate to the Ticket Editor and select **Tank Gauge**.

5.  Right-click the grid and select **New Ticket**.

6.  Navigate to the **Ticket Search**.

7.  Right-click the grid and select **New Ticket** \> **Tank Gauge**.

8.  Edit the date as appropriate.

9.  Select the product from the list. If the tank has been set up with a list of valid products, only those will appear in the drop-down. If a default product was specified, it will be pre-selected in the drop-down.

10. Enter tank gauging information. Data points are different for each tank type.

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Upright Cylindrical Tank Guage Tickets">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Upright Cylindrical Tank Gauge Tickets</a>

    <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Upright Cylindrical Tank Guage Tickets">

    If a CTSh is to be calculated, ambient temperature is required, and the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Apply Shell Temperature Correction, CTSh’ enabled. If the option to calculate CTSh is not enabled, or FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CTSh, then a value of one is assumed.

    S&W % is not required. If S&W % is not specified, zero is assumed.

    Free Water is not required. If Free Water is not specified, zero is assumed.

    If CTSh, FRA, or CTL is provided on import, these values will be stored into revision 0, but the calculations will use the FLOWCAL calculated CTSh, FRA, or CTL; however, if a user manually enters CTSh, FRA, or CTL, then FLOWCAL will use the manually entered values in the calculations.

    </div>

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Horizontal Tank Gauge Tickets">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Horizontal Tank Gauge Tickets</a>

    <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Horizontal Tank Gauge Tickets">

    If a Correction for Shell Temperature is to be calculated, the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Use Steel Temperature Correction (CTS) for Calculations’ enabled. If the option to calculate CTS is not enabled, or FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CTS, then a value of one is assumed.

    If CTS or CTL is provided on import, these values will be stored into revision 0, but the calculations will use the FLOWCAL calculated CTS or CTL; however, if a user manually enters CTS or CTL, then FLOWCAL will use the manually entered values in the calculations.

    In order to calculate Vapor Density, observed density, observed temperature, and analysis are needed.

    </div>

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Spherical Tank Gauge Tickets">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Spherical Tank Gauge Tickets</a>

    <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Spherical Tank Gauge Tickets">

    If a CTS liquid/CTS vapor is to be calculated, tank construction material and liquid/vapor temperature are needed, and the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Use Steel Temperature Correction (CTS) for Calculations’ enabled. If the option to use CTS is not enabled, then a value of one is assumed. If the option to use CTS is enabled and FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CTS, CTS is not calculated.

    If a CPS is to be calculated, tank construction material, thickness of tank shell, and tank pressure are needed, and the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Use Steel Pressure Correction (CPS) for Calculations’ enabled. If the option to use CPS is not enabled, then a value of one is assumed. If the option to use CTS is enabled and FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CPS, CPS is not calculated.

    Spherical tank does not support sediment and water. Even if S&W% is provided on analysis, 0% sediment and water is assumed for calculation.

    In order to calculate Vapor Density, observed density, observed temperature, observed pressure, and analysis are needed.

    If CTS liquid, CTS vapor, or CTL is provided on import, these values will be stored into revision 0, but the calculations will use the FLOWCAL calculated CTS liquid, CTS vapor, or CTL; however, if a user manually enters CTS liquid, CTS vapor, or CTL, then FLOWCAL will use the manually entered values in the calculations.

    </div>

11. Click **Calculate** to see the results.

12. Enter data on the **Accounting**, **Analysis**, **Components**, and **Custom Fields** tabs as needed.

13. Select an edit reason.

14. Click **Save**. Data will calculate and save to the database.

15. Click **Exit**.
